## Summary
WhatTheyThink coverage of Cober Solutions (Canadian printer, ~103-year-old family business) hitting 20% growth in print-on-demand revenue 18 months after deploying Infigo (Apr 2020). The article reads as third-party trade-press confirmation of Infigo's own case-study claims; Erwin Driever (VP Technology at Cober) is the named source.

## Key takeaways
- **Deployment timeline:** Signed up April 2020. 20% on-demand revenue growth reported at the 18-month mark (~Oct 2021).
- **Tech stack integration documented:** Infigo + Tharstern MIS + internal workflow / automation / payment / shipping. Notable that ALL of: orders, payments, manufacturing, shipping run "with minimal human intervention" — useful integration-completeness benchmark.
- **Driving force was new customer demand, not cost-cutting:** Cober "acquired and onboarded a number of new clients from some major brands" specifically because of what Infigo could offer. This is a pattern-match for the shop's enterprise-storefront pitch.
- **Pre-Infigo experience:** Cober had been doing W2P for 15+ years across multiple vendors. Switched to Infigo because they needed "highly complex variable data composition and automation" — the prior vendors couldn't meet the complexity bar.
- **Why this is a credible third-party signal:** Cober is a real, traceable Canadian company (mentioned across PrintAction, WTT, BusinessWire); HP Indigo 100K press buyer; not an Infigo-paid mouthpiece. The 20% growth figure has appeared across multiple independent trade outlets.
